clue.text: Former emperor finished with such a girl

indicators.note: the emperor's name finishes with the girl, so only its closing run of letters is kept

parts.note: Haile Selassie was the last Emperor of Ethiopia

explanation.surface: A deposed emperor has finished with a particular young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished with' reads as dropping the girl, but it means the emperor's name ends with her: SELASSIE loses its opening SE. LASSIE is Scottish and northern English for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass or young woman in Scots usage is exactly this kind of girl.

clue.text: Way of approaching a rendezvous

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to get to an arranged meeting point.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a means or route of approach, as in exploring every avenue.

clue.text: TV programme bosses lacking time, in such a lather

parts.note: a soap opera, a soap, is a TV programme

indicators.note: lacking says the word for bosses goes without the letter for time

parts.note: bosses are ornamental knobs, studs

explanation.surface: Television executives, short of time, are in a frantic state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosses' looks like managers but means studs, raised knobs; without T that leaves SUDS. 'in such a lather' plays on lather as agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy froth is a lather, so the foam is literally such a lather.

clue.text: All of us English extremely united

parts.note: extremely means very
united means at one, so one

explanation.surface: Patriotic claim that the English are wholly as one.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun naming every person present covers all of us.

clue.text: Money needed before one can cut mustard, say

indicators.note: before places the money ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: cut means the word can loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: You need cash before you can be good enough, cut the mustard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut mustard' looks like the idiom for being good enough; 'cut' trims CAN to CA, and 'mustard, say' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is one plant of the cabbage genus, an example of the brassica group.

clue.text: Another author from Jane Austen's family, say

indicators.note: say signals that the family name is heard and spelt another way

parts.note: the Bennets are the family in Pride and Prejudice

explanation.surface: Another writer descended from Jane Austen's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jane Austen's family' is not her own relatives but her fictional Bennet family; Alan Bennett is a British playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett is a well-known English writer, so he is a further author.

clue.text: Icons are laid out differently for outline sketch

indicators.note: laid out differently says the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Desktop icons are rearranged to form a rough design.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a plot outline or sketch of a possible course of events.

clue.text: Stars and Stripes, for example

parts.note: not the US flag but stars and stripes as military badges of rank

explanation.surface: The American flag given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges such as officers' stars and NCOs' stripes are emblems of rank.

clue.text: Work in church making convert calm, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks the phrase as spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: convert means alter and calm means peace

explanation.surface: A church project that brings tranquillity to converts.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or carving behind the communion table is a work of art in a church.

clue.text: Marine mammal' caught by Greek character at sea, nonetheless

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: read as none-less: the word for sea loses its O, a nought or none

parts.note: the ocean is the sea

explanation.surface: A sea creature taken by a Greek out on the water anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' looks like 'however', but splits as none-less: the word for sea minus its nought, a zero or none. 'at sea' is a red herring suggesting an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales, dolphins and porpoises form the order of sea mammals so named.

clue.text: China to aggravate Taiwanese leader

parts.note: to tease is to annoy or aggravate

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leader, first letter, of Taiwanese is T

explanation.surface: Beijing sets out to annoy the head of Taiwan.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery, or china, for serving afternoon tea comes as a matching set of cups and saucers.

clue.text: Risk death by Fury

parts.note: death is the end
fury is anger

explanation.surface: A warning that rage could bring about death.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something at risk is to imperil it.

clue.text: Admiral who scaled stronghold with escort

parts.note: a beau is a male escort or suitor
a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: A naval commander climbed a fortress with his companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaled' suggests climbing; it means devising a scale: Admiral Beaufort gave his name to the wind-force scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Beaufort was the naval officer who drew up the wind-force scale.

clue.text: Boycott a drug distributed for villain

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as in trade-union usage

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A drug dealer who should be shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges A DRUG to GUARD. 'Boycott' may suggest the Yorkshire cricketer; it is the verb, to black.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel or rogue is an old-fashioned villain.

clue.text: A requirement, one's gathered, -for making ouzo

indicators.note: gathered means the word for need takes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: a requirement is a need
one's is I'S, the numeral I plus S

explanation.surface: Something required, a single one collected, in making a Greek spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzo is a Greek spirit flavoured with the seed of anise, the ingredient needed to make it.

clue.text: Capital strangely unsuitable, apart from the outskirts

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters are put in an odd new order
apart from the outskirts drops the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A capital city rated, oddly, as unfit except for its suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from the outskirts' strips U and E from UNSUITABLE, leaving NSUITABL, which 'strangely' rearranges. It was the Ottoman capital, and 'capital' here means a chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly Constantinople, it was the capital city of the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: With one or two starting off, sex occurs thus, as a digression

indicators.text: With one or two starting off
indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first one or two letters

explanation.surface: A risqué aside about how intercourse begins, offered as a tangent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With one or two starting off' takes S from sex, OC from occurs and TH from thus, leaving EX, CURS and US.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin term for an extended aside or appended discussion in a text.

clue.text: Thus dead after current is cut off

indicators.note: after puts the pieces for thus and dead behind the current

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
so means thus
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Something dies once the electricity is switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or seal off from others.

clue.text: Confess about crush, describing beautiful girl

indicators.note: about means the word for confess goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
to mash is to crush

explanation.surface: Admitting to a crush on a lovely girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' looks like infatuation, but is the verb, to mash.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for wonderful or very attractive, a word used of a lovely girl.

clue.text: Manage to get dispatch showing our country's extreme position

parts.note: to land something is to manage to get it
to dispatch is to send

explanation.surface: Getting a posting to the far corner of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: LAND'S END is the westernmost tip of mainland England, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish headland is the far western extremity of England.

clue.text: Make progress with velocity in a hop, say

indicators.note: in places the velocity letter within the other pieces

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance, given as an example
V is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: Moving forward quickly with a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To go forward or progress is to move ahead.

clue.text: A garden I transformed — with this?

definitions.text: A garden I transformed — with this?

indicators.note: transformed means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking what would be needed to remake a soggy garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a garden transformed might well need this.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying pipes or ditches to carry off water is how a waterlogged plot is improved.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about grass producing beard

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the grass

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a lawn that has grown into a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed tuft of hair on the chin is a kind of beard.

clue.text: Composer, little good and mostly idle, taking duos from unfinished overtures

parts.note: a little good is its abbreviation G

indicators.note: mostly means the word for idle loses its last letter

parts.note: idle means lazy

indicators.note: duos means pairs of letters taken from the start of each word

explanation.surface: A lazy composer who left his overtures unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking duos from' takes the first two letters of unfinished and overtures, UN and OV. Glazunov was a Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Glazunov was a Russian Romantic composer.

clue.text: Jump with surprise

definitions.meaning: to jump someone is to attack them suddenly
to surprise an enemy is to take them unawares

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe attacking from hiding, a sudden attack that takes victims unawares.

clue.text: In informal letter, I put "sweetie"

indicators.note: In means the following pieces go inside the letter

parts.note: a note is a short informal letter
to set is to put

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a casual note to a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetie' looks like a term of endearment; it is a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a chocolate made with hazelnuts, a sweet.

clue.text: Delaware to be found outside America? Unreal

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware

indicators.note: outside means the word for exist goes round the country

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
US is America

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a US state could exist beyond America.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deceptive or illusory is unreal.

clue.text: Go in search of pleasure and procure ingenious device

parts.note: to gad about is to go out seeking fun
to procure is to get

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker going out to buy a clever gizmo.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a clever little contrivance or tool.
